chunks: "I'd think of it as an optimisation problem with three main pieces.
First, the order of placements: the head has to travel from the feeders to each spot on the board, and finding the shortest path through all of them is basically a travelling salesman problem.
A good heuristic, like nearest neighbour followed by two-opt improvement, can cut the travel by large factors compared with an arbitrary order.
Second, feeder assignment: put the most-used parts on the feeders closest to the board, and put parts that are picked together next to each other so a multi-nozzle head can collect several in one go.

Third, reduce non-travel overhead: group parts by nozzle type to minimise nozzle changes, use collect-and-place heads so you make fewer trips, and balance the load over several machines on the line so none is the bottleneck.
On the design side, fewer unique part values and common package sizes mean fewer feeders and fewer nozzle changes, and panelising boards means the same optimised path repeats.
In practice the machine vendor's software does the heavy lifting, but I'd still check that the result is balanced."
